newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF group sees 3-mth euro based on EMU benchmark.
newsitem.headline: MATIF group sees 3-mth euro based on EMU benchmark.

text.p: A working group set up by MATIF futures and options exchange recommended the listing of a three-month interest rate future in euros based on new benchmark rates set by banks within a single currency zone.

A report released on Wednesday on the transition to a planned single currency in 1999, said "The working committee recommends that the three-month euro contract be given an EMU (European monetary union) benchmark.
It said the new benchmark rates should be set by "a panel of 20-30 banks of member states of the currency zone, presenting a homogenous rating".

The development of the benchmark would depend on which countries participated in the first round of monetary union but it said there was no reason why an EMU benchmark could not exist in conjunction with an "offshore" market in London.

"Should the United Kingdom not join EMU, or should obligatory reserves be imposed on banks inside the EMU zone, the European money market could be divided between a continental and an offshore market, which would justify the existence of two distinct benchmarks," the report said.

The continental benchmark "could be the result either of giving a European banking base to the PIBOR benchmark calculated by the Association of French banks, or EMU banks constructing an ad hoc panel", it said.

Jacques Werren, deputy managing director of MATIF, said "London enjoys a strong position as an offshore market place. The question is more to predict whether the euro is to be more a domestic kind of currency or an international one. It is an open question I believe."
